personas.name: Mira, the puzzle parent
personas.who: 44, works full time, plays on an older phone in portrait at the end of the day. Plays the Ratel as a casual puzzle game; gets pulled into her son Jonah's squad on weekends.
personas.challenge: The example runs the wrong way round in today's build. The Ratel is not a game she can find: it is the second seat of the Honeyguide, reached through the Toybox's Vessel Changer and a two-finger swipe. So she cannot start as a solo puzzle player and later be roped in. She is roped in first, by Jonah, and only discovers the Ratel because it is the one seat that needs no flying. And his squad cannot take her along: the Honeyguide has no arena card, so the day he moves to the arena she is handed a hull to fly.

fate.why: She can only reach the Ratel when Jonah sets it up, and on day 13 he takes the squad to the arena, where the Honeyguide has no card. She flies a Squirrel, finishes last, and stops.

steps.note: Jonah installs it on her phone and asks her into his party.

personas.name: Jonah, the squad kid
personas.who: 14, plays after school on a PC and his phone, watches clips of the game, wants every hull. The one who pulls his mother in.
personas.challenge: He is the engine of Mira's path, so his path decides hers. Today he gets every card on day 1 under the master unlock and burns through the fleet's novelty in two weeks; when he leaves, Mira goes with him. With the activation gate flipped he would instead be held for hours behind a quest chain that ends at I4, which is too slow for him in the other direction.

fate.why: Everything was open on day 1 and nothing has changed since. By week 4 his friends have moved to another game and he follows.

personas.name: The night crew
personas.who: Four friends, 24 to 28, on PC with voice chat. The arena most nights from about 21:30, voyages in a long binge on Saturday afternoons.
personas.challenge: Four does not fit. An arena team is three seats and a voyage party is at most three players, so every night one of them is on the other team or out. Only the winner of a match is paid (200 crystals, 4000 a vessel), so in a group that wins and loses to each other the quietest friend owns nothing new after two weeks. A Saturday voyage binge builds only the host's Ark and hoard. And they never meet activation at all: they come in by invite and go straight to the arena, which is fine today and would be a wall if the gate flipped as planned.

fate.why: The quietest friend leaves on day 17. By day 30 the top two own the priced fleet and crystals buy nothing; the arena has not changed since day 1. Nights drop to two a week and the crew moves to another game.

personas.name: The five-minute commuter
personas.from: Claude, to challenge the Session tier
personas.who: 34, rides a train twice a day on an older Android phone, sound off, one hand. Six or seven minutes a sitting.
personas.challenge: The atlas's Session tier starts at 10 minutes and a voyage takes 20 to 40. His sittings are 6. Most of the game is out of reach of his day: he can fit three Time rounds and nothing that banks. He is the player the economy simulation's short-session cultures will look like.

fate.why: Twelve days of the same three cards. Nothing between his sittings carries over except crystals at 200 a win, a vessel 20 wins away, and the voyage he tried on day 4 cannot be paused.
